subject: Request: short extension + promotional uplift for Nebula Health bake-off
messages:

To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 13:02:00 -0000
Subject: Nebula bake-off: short extension + ask for promotional uplift

Hi Lukas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's latency profile and the KV cache story. We just received an internal ask from procurement: the evaluation window in our RFP was set to close this Friday, but our engineering team needs two extra business days to run the side-by-side with competitor X.

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood grant a short 48-hour extension on the free trial credit (we estimate ~120k tokens extra)?
- Would Redwood consider a small promotional uplift (an additional 50k evaluation credit) if we include Redwood as a preferred vendor line-item in the RFP scoreboard?

I've attached the RFP summary and our rough usage estimates. Procurement is on cc (procurement@nebulahq.com). We need an answer by EOD Monday to update scoring timelines.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Alex Ruiz
Head of ML Platforms
Nebula Health

Ben / Marissa — forwarding Nebula's ask. Quick summary: 48-hour trial extension + ask for +50k promo credit in return for preferred-vendor visibility on their RFP scoreboard. They estimate ~120k tokens for the extra two days.

My thought: we can grant the extension and consider a small uplift if we gate it to a win/shortlist — keep it conditional. Pricing cap and ops guardrails needed (SLA, token burn cap).

Key questions:
- Ben: capacity impact on Dedicated/shared pools that week? any risk of noisy neighbor?
- Marissa: approval for promo uplift — this feels like an upsell nudge. Do we need leader approval or can you sign off?

I'll reply to Alex once we have internal alignment.

Looks reasonable to me. Operational notes:
- 120k tokens over 48 hours is negligible for hosted but if Nebula bursts to parallel long sequences we should route to lower-cost variant to preserve latency SLOs. I can set a soft throttle and a KV prefix cache for the test prompt set.
- We should pin model version and set a token cap with automatic pause + ops alert.

Credit ask: 50k promo credit is fine as a conditional incentive — recommend we make it contingent on them sharing final scoreboard (to prove shortlisting) and signing a short AMP (pilot acceptance) doc.

I'll preconfigure the throttle and a temporary policy. If Marissa signs off on the promo, we can authorize in HubSpot and I will apply the credit.

Ben
Sales Engineering

Alex / team —

Thanks for the clear ask and for the attachments. We can do the following:
1) Grant a 48-hour extension to your evaluation window (adds two business days) and provision an additional 120k evaluation token allotment to cover the extended testing window.
2) Issue a conditional 50k promotional credit (applied to your HubSpot trial account) under these written conditions: you add Redwood as a preferred-vendor line-item on the RFP scoreboard and share the final scoreboard PDF with us within 14 days of award announcement. The credit expires 30 days after issuance if unused.

Next steps:
- Alex: confirm you accept the conditional terms and provide a short PO reference if procurement needs it.
- Procurement: if you need a one-line note for internal scorekeeping confirming the conditional promo, I can provide a signed note from Sales Ops.

I have attached a draft proposal for internal HubSpot (redwood-proposal-draft.docx) and linked the HubSpot deal below. Once procurement gives the thumbs up we'll apply the credits and send a short AMP (pilot acceptance) agreement.

HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.company/deal/HB-2027-0098
